key_insight: ZO-Act improves zeroth-order fine-tuning by restricting perturbations to a fixed activation-informed low-rank subspace, lowering estimator variance while enabling efficient forward-only optimization.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to fine-tune large and even quantized LLMs without backpropagation, reducing memory pressure and making Adam-like optimization available in a ZO setting.
method: Compute a small activation basis once per linear layer at initialization.
Optimize lightweight coefficient matrices instead of full weights or random subspaces.
Use forward-only loss evaluations with a restricted coefficient-space ZO estimator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over strong ZO baselines on Llama-3-8B, OPT-13B, and INT4 Llama-3-8B across language understanding, QA, and commonsense reasoning.
watch_item: Performance still depends on how well the low-rank activation subspace approximates the true gradient directions, so poor basis quality can introduce approximation bias.
paper_title: ZO-Act: Efficient Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning via One-Shot Activation-Informed Low-Rank Subspaces
